result:
I wrote `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/ArrayUtilsAgentTest.java` with 81 self-contained test methods covering `ArrayUtils`'s major method families (add/addAll/addFirst, clone, concat, contains/containsAny, get, getLength/getComponentType, hashCode, indexesOf/indexOf/lastIndexOf, insert, isArrayIndexValid/isEmpty/isEquals/isSameLength/isSameType/isSorted, newInstance, nullTo/nullToEmpty, remove/removeAll/removeAllOccurrence(s)/removeElement(s), reverse, shift, startsWith, subarray, swap, toArray/toMap/toObject/toPrimitive/toString(Array), and the `EMPTY_*` constants), including boundary cases (negative/out-of-range indices, null arrays, empty arrays, tolerance comparisons).

All 81 tests pass against the current `ArrayUtils` implementation — I found no bugs. During development three of my initial assertions turned out to be wrong assumptions rather than code bugs, and I corrected them to match the documented contract:
- `get(array, index)` (2-arg) returns `null` for an out-of-bounds index/null array rather than throwing (per its Javadoc).
- `insert(index, null, values)` returns `null` for a `null` array (per its Javadoc), not a newly built array.
- `hashCode(null)` is not documented to be `0`; it delegates to `HashCodeBuilder`, which returns a fixed non-zero constant — I only assert it's deterministic, not a specific value.
